mainTopic: 亲子关系与青春期沟通
mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕“同一屋檐下的陌生人”话题，涵盖亲子冲突的成因（Reading）、家庭带来的安全感（Extended reading）和压力倾诉与求助（Integrated skills）三个子话题，均为高考应用文与雅思议论文的高频命题区。

subTopics.title: 亲子冲突与沟通之道
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：争吵与冷战的成因、the key to keeping the peace，以及换位思考的沟通建议。

prompts.task: 假设你是李华。你的英国笔友 Tom 来信说，他最近因手机使用问题频繁与父母发生激烈争吵（heated arguments），甚至冷战，感到十分苦恼。请你写一封回信，内容包括：1. 表示理解并分析这类冲突的原因；2. 给出两条具体的沟通建议；3. 表达鼓励。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Tom,

I'm sorry to hear that every dinner at your home seems to turn into a battle. Please don't feel alone — heated arguments and cold silences are common between teenagers and their parents, because we have both a new desire for independence and a continued need to be looked after.

Here is my advice. First, when it all gets too much, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from your parents' point of view. Second, after you have thought it through, explain your feelings calmly and address their concerns about your screen time.

Just remember that growing up is a rough ride, and regular and honest communication is the key to keeping the peace. I'm sure things will turn out all right.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: the key to keeping the peace

prompts.task: Some people believe that conflicts between teenagers and their parents are harmful and should be avoided, while others think such conflicts are a natural and even necessary part of growing up. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Disagreements between adolescents and their parents are as old as family life itself. While some observers regard these clashes as damaging episodes that families should strive to prevent, others see them as an inevitable, even constructive, feature of the journey to adulthood. On balance, I believe that such friction, when handled with care, does more good than harm.

Those who wish to avoid conflict altogether have understandable concerns. Repeated quarrels can poison the atmosphere at home, leaving both sides exhausted and resentful. If a disagreement hardens into a prolonged cold war, communication may break down entirely, and the young person may stop seeking guidance at precisely the age when it is most needed. From this standpoint, harmony appears worth protecting at almost any cost.

The opposing camp, however, argues that a measure of friction is simply the growing pains of independence. Teenagers are developing their own tastes, opinions and boundaries, and testing these against parental authority is how they learn to negotiate, compromise and defend a position with reasons rather than tears. A household that permits respectful disagreement, in this view, is actually rehearsing its children for adult life, where differences of opinion cannot be wished away.

In my judgement, the second position is the more convincing, with one proviso: conflict is only productive when it ends in honest conversation rather than slammed doors. Parents who listen before they lecture, and teenagers who explain rather than explode, can turn an argument into an exchange of perspectives. Friction, in other words, is not the enemy of family bonds; silence is.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):完整覆盖 discuss both views + own opinion——引言末句亮明立场('does more good than harm')并加限定('when handled with care'),第二段陈述'冲突有害论'及其推演(争吵→冷战→沟通断裂),第三段陈述'冲突必要论'并论证(试探边界→学会协商),结论段重申立场且补充条件(proviso),立场贯穿不摇摆。

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):四段各有单一中心;衔接自然多样——'Those who wish to avoid...'、'The opposing camp, however'、'From this standpoint'、'In my judgement',不堆砌 Firstly/Secondly;末句'Friction is not the enemy; silence is'以对照收束,首尾呼应。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):地道搭配密集——'poison the atmosphere'、'hardens into a prolonged cold war'、'the growing pains of independence'、'rehearsing its children for adult life'、'listen before they lecture / explain rather than explode'(双头韵对句);近义替换灵活(clashes/friction/quarrels/disagreement)。

Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性与准确性):句式多样——条件从句('If a disagreement hardens into...')、非限定从句('where differences of opinion cannot be wished away')、插入语('in this view')、with 独立结构('with one proviso')、分词短语('leaving both sides exhausted');几乎零错误。

subTopics.title: 家庭与安全感
subTopics.desc: 《妈妈的银行账户》：一个“并不存在的账户”给全家人带来安全感——家庭如何成为孩子的底气。

prompts.task: 你校英文报正举办以 "What Family Means to Me" 为主题的征文活动。请你结合自己或身边人的经历写一篇短文投稿，内容包括：1. 家庭给你的安全感体现在何处；2. 一件具体的小事；3. 你的感悟。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Whatever happens, I always know I still have my family to depend upon — that is what family means to me.

Last winter, I failed an important exam and dared not mention it at dinner. My mother said nothing about marks. Instead, she put an extra bowl of my favourite soup in front of me and said, "Eat first. Everything will turn out all right." That warm, secure feeling stayed with me for the whole evening, and I went back to my books with fresh courage.

Family, I have learned, is not a place where we are never judged; it is a place where we are always received. Like a bank account that never runs out, its love is something we can draw upon in every emergency.
vocabHints: draw money out of an account

prompts.task: Some people believe that the family has the greatest influence on a child's development, while others think that outside factors such as friends, school and the media play a more important role. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
What shapes a child most decisively — the home or the wider world — remains a subject of lively debate. Some hold that the family exerts the deepest influence on a young person's development, while others contend that friends, schooling and the media now matter more. In my view, although outside forces grow louder with age, the family remains the quiet foundation on which everything else is built.

Supporters of the second position make a persuasive case. From adolescence onwards, children spend the greater part of their waking hours away from home, absorbing the values of classmates and the messages of a screen-saturated culture. Peer approval can outweigh parental advice; a trend on social media can reshape a teenager's tastes overnight. Judged purely by hours of exposure, the outside world seems to hold the stronger hand.

Yet influence is not measured by volume alone. The family provides what no algorithm or classmate can: an unconditional sense of security. A child who knows there is always someone to depend upon acquires the confidence to explore, fail and try again. Habits of honesty, patience and care are rehearsed at the dinner table long before they are tested in public. Even the way young people handle friendship and criticism tends to mirror the emotional patterns first learned at home.

On balance, therefore, I side with those who place the family first. External voices may decorate the building of character, but the foundations are poured early, at home, and in silence. When those foundations are sound, the louder world can influence a child without ever owning them.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):三问全答——引言即立立场('the family remains the quiet foundation'),第二段公允展开对方论据(时间占比/同伴认同/社媒),第三段以'影响不以音量计'反转并纵深论证(安全感→敢于试错→情感模式镜像),结论权衡收束,立场首尾一致。

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):'Supporters of the second position...'、'Yet influence is not measured by volume alone'、'On balance, therefore'层层推进;建筑隐喻(foundation→decorate the building→foundations are poured)贯穿三段,成为全文的衔接暗线。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):'a screen-saturated culture'、'hold the stronger hand'、'an unconditional sense of security'、'rehearsed at the dinner table'、'influence a child without ever owning them'——搭配新鲜准确;depend upon/security 等词呼应话题而不显堆砌。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):破折号插入定义式开头、冒号引出核心概念('provides what no algorithm or classmate can: ...')、关系从句与分词交替使用;长短句节奏明显(第三段末双短句收势),错误几乎为零。

语域:学术客观语气,隐喻服务论证而非抒情;高考征文鼓励温情叙事和抒情结尾。

subTopics.title: 别活在比较里
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：There's no point in comparing you with others all the time、seek expert advice、it is likely that——青少年健康论坛给出的第一条建议，往往是先放下比较。

prompts.task: 你校英文报开设 "Growing Pains" 专栏。请你写一篇短文，谈谈如何摆脱总和别人比较的焦虑，内容包括：1. 现象与危害；2. 你的两三条建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Many of us know the feeling: a classmate scores higher, dresses better or has more friends, and suddenly our own life seems to lose its colour. But there is no point in comparing yourself with others all the time.

So what can we do? First, remember that it is likely that the person you envy is quietly comparing themselves with someone else, too. Second, measure your progress against your own past, not against other people. Finally, if the pressure feels too heavy, do not be afraid to seek expert advice from a teacher or counsellor.

Comparison steals joy. The moment we stop running someone else's race, we finally start winning our own.
vocabHints: there is no point in comparing yourself with others

prompts.task: Some people believe that comparing themselves with others motivates people to work harder and improve, while others think it mainly causes anxiety and unhappiness. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Human beings measure themselves against one another almost instinctively. Some regard this habit as a healthy engine of ambition; others see it as a reliable source of misery. Having weighed both positions, I believe comparison can motivate, but only when it is aimed carefully, and that in most everyday cases it does more harm than good.

Those who defend comparison have a point. Seeing a peer succeed can prove that a goal is achievable and supply a concrete standard to aim for; athletes train harder beside stronger rivals, and students often raise their game when surrounded by ambitious classmates. Used as information — what is possible, and how — comparison can sharpen effort.

Yet the same habit easily turns corrosive. Most comparison is not analytical but emotional, and it fixes on the narrow areas where others appear ahead while ignoring everything else. Social media has magnified the damage, parading edited highlights of other lives until ordinary people feel like failures by contrast. The result is anxiety, envy and, ironically, less energy for genuine improvement, because self-doubt paralyses more often than it inspires.

The decisive difference lies in the object of comparison. Comparing methods and results with others can be useful; comparing one's worth with theirs rarely is. The healthier reference point is one's own earlier self, a measure that records real progress without breeding resentment.

In conclusion, while measuring ourselves against others can occasionally spur us on, it more often undermines confidence and contentment. The wiser path is to learn from others' achievements yet to judge success by how far we ourselves have come.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点均展开(激励方:目标可达/同伴效应;伤害方:情感性比较/社媒放大/自我怀疑瘫痪)，立场'方式性比较有用、价值性比较有害+以过去的自己为参照'精确细分，不停在'看情况'。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):a healthy engine of ambition / turns corrosive / parading edited highlights / breeding resentment / spur us on 等表达精准且带评价色彩。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):until结果状语、分号对举、not A but B(not analytical but emotional)、while让步开启结论，句式多样零硬伤。

subTopics.title: 青春期压力与倾诉
subTopics.desc: 课件情景：被父母催促学习（keep pressing me to study）、渴望喘息（take a break once in a while）与希望父母更灵活（more flexible）的心声。

prompts.task: 你班将举行以 "Less Pressure, Better Life" 为主题的班会。请你准备一篇发言稿，谈谈中学生如何应对来自父母期望的压力，内容包括：1. 压力的表现；2. 你的两条应对建议；3. 呼吁。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Good afternoon, everyone!

Many of us feel that our parents keep pressing us to study all the time. We understand their love, yet the stress can sometimes be killing us, and we wish they could be more flexible so that we could make our own choices.

How should we respond? First, talk instead of exploding. Choose a calm moment, tell them how you feel, and let them know you also value your future. Second, allow yourself to take a break once in a while — a short walk or a game of basketball works wonders for a tired mind.

Pressure is part of growing up, but it should push us forward, not weigh us down. Let's face it with honest words and a light heart. Thank you!

prompts.task: In many countries, teenagers today experience more academic pressure than previous generations. What are the causes of this problem? What measures could be taken to solve it? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Few would dispute that today's teenagers carry a heavier academic load than their parents ever did. Understanding why this pressure has intensified — and how it might be relieved — has become an urgent question for families, schools and governments alike.

Two causes stand out. The first is competition inflated by scale: higher education has expanded, yet the most desirable universities and careers remain scarce, so each examination is treated as a gateway that must not be missed. The second cause lies closer to home. Many parents, anxious for their children to succeed in a fast-changing economy, translate their own insecurity into relentless supervision — extra classes, constant monitoring and little tolerance for rest. Add the glow of social media, where every peer's achievement is on display, and an ordinary school day begins to feel like a public race.

Solutions must therefore work on both fronts. At the policy level, schools can broaden what counts as success, giving weight to projects, arts and service rather than a single test score, so that one narrow gate becomes several doors. Equally important are changes within the family: parents who schedule genuine free time, praise effort rather than ranking, and listen before they advise can turn the home from a second classroom back into a place of recovery. Simple habits — regular exercise, enough sleep, an evening free of screens — cost nothing and measurably lower stress.

Academic pressure will never disappear, nor should it entirely; a degree of challenge makes growth possible. The task is to keep pressure at a level where it sharpens young minds instead of breaking them.

Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):破折号插入、倒装('Equally important are changes...')、祈使式列举('Add the glow of...')、非限定从句与分词短语交替;因果链条句(so that.../where...)准确无误。
